questions.stem: What is the SI unit of weight?
questions.explanation: Weight is a force (the gravitational pull on an object), so it is measured in newtons (N). Mass is measured in kilograms (kg). This is one of the most common errors in physics.

questions.stem: An astronaut has a mass of 70 kg. What happens to their mass and weight when they travel to the Moon (where g = 1.6 m/s²)?

options.text: Mass stays the same, weight decreases
Mass decreases, weight stays the same
Both mass and weight stay the same

questions.explanation: Mass is a property of the object and does not change with location -- it remains 70 kg. Weight depends on the gravitational field strength, so on the Moon: W = mg = 70 x 1.6 = 112 N (much less than on Earth).
